notable_absence.finding: TWO separate docs issues on one short page. (1) Role-naming drift: this page's Required Permissions section says 'Full Amin, Backup Admin, or Read-Only Admin' - 'Full Amin' is a typo for 'Full Admin', and 'Backup Admin' is a THIRD spelling of the role the overview page's tables imply and backup-get-task-info.md / backup-node-threads.md both call 'Backup Full Admin'. roles.md's own catalogue names it 'Backup Full Admin (backup_admin)' - so 'Backup Admin' here is neither the display label nor the internal name, it's a third, unofficial shorthand. Resolved to the same role:backup-full-admin id since the internal name backup_admin is unambiguous, but the inconsistency is worth a docs ticket. (2) The parent backup-rest-api.md's Configuration table lists THREE methods for /api/v1/config - GET, POST, and PUT - but this page, whose whole job is to document that endpoint, only ever mentions GET and POST. PUT is never shown in an HTTP Methods and URIs section, a curl example, or a Required Permissions line anywhere on this page. Either the overview table is wrong, or this page is missing a third of its own subject matter.

cross_component_finding: This page has no relationship to cbbackupmgr at all - history_rotation_size is a Backup-Service-only setting (how much of the SERVICE's own task-history log to retain) with no CLI equivalent found in any cbbackupmgr reference page extracted so far, unlike backup:retention-period and backup:pruning which this batch's backup-retention.md and backup-trigger-prune.md show are genuinely shared REST/CLI-adjacent concepts. This is useful negative evidence for the round's central question: not every Backup-Service REST concept maps onto something cbbackupmgr already has a name for. The service's own operational housekeeping (its history log, its thread count) is Backup-Service-specific; the data it manages (repositories, backups, plans) is the shared layer with cbbackupmgr.
